conviction_note: abs_move 20 (option-implied event move 14.9%, own median reaction 21.9% over 7 verified prints, first guide update of the new fiscal year, 18% of float short) x (2*0.57-1) = +2.8; the findings sum to +5.0 because the decisive positives (disclosed orders already cover the low end of the FY27 guide; the lead Sonoma customer re-ordered the day after Teradyne's Titan HP launch) are company documents, while p_up is held at 57 rather than 60+ because the put skew (+11.75 vol pts) and a -49% 20-day tape say the market expects more bad news and an Oppenheimer rebuttal on Oct 14 already failed to stop the slide.
bar: Q1 FY2027 (13 weeks, 2026-06-27 to 2026-09-25) revenue ~$26.6-27.5M and EPS $0.10-0.11: Zacks $27.5M / $0.11 (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:92d98440e094b:0-aehr-gears-up-to-report-q1-earnings-what-s-in-store-for-the-stock/), Investing.com/Reuters $26.82M / $0.1025, 6 analysts (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/aehr-test-systems-earnings-on-deck-amid-ai-chip-boom-93CH-4990455), MarketBeat $26.6M (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-11-2-aehr-test-systems-stock/). Three sources agree within 3%. No company Q1 guide; the company guide is FY2027 revenue $130-150M with non-GAAP pretax income 18-22% of revenue (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001040470/000165495426006655/aehr_ex991.htm, 2026-07-14). The 10-Q will also carry a 28-day transition period (2026-05-30 to 06-26) with 'minimal shipments' and $20M of bookings.
positioning_check: Short interest 5,622,469 shares = 18.05% of float, days to cover 2.0, settlement 2026-10-15, up 7.7% from 5,220,478 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/AEHR/short-interest/, read 2026-11-02). Baseline: 25-delta skew +11.75 vol pts (downside paid), put/call OI 0.5, ATM IV 183.7%, event-implied move 14.89%, run-up 20d -48.97%, 5d -5.87%, 63% off the 52w high ($147.40 on 2026-08-14). Crowded short into a stock that has already halved, but the skew still pays for downside.

findings.finding: Disclosed orders already cover roughly the low end of the FY2027 revenue guide ($130-150M): the effective backlog of $100.6M on 2026-07-14 ($80.6M backlog at 2026-05-29 plus $20M booked in the transition period), plus a $22M AI-processor wafer-level burn-in order (2026-08-12) and ~$6M of Sonoma follow-on orders (2026-10-07), comes to about $128.6M before the undisclosed silicon-photonics follow-on (2026-07-09) and any SiC or other bookings. The market reads the guide as at risk after a 49% drawdown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints, each carrying record bookings or a backlog/guide step-up, were bought: +21.91% (2026-07-14, record $60.7M bookings and a first FY27 guide), +25.69% (2026-04-07, $37.2M orders despite a revenue miss), +15.95% (2026-01-08). Prints where order timing slipped were sold: -17.38% (2025-10-06), -12.39% (2025-07-08).
findings.why_not_priced: If the market believed the guide were covered, the stock would not have halved in 20 sessions to about 12x the guide's midpoint revenue, with puts bid at +11.75 vol pts. The arithmetic needs three separate company releases (Jul 14 8-K, Aug 12 and Oct 7 PRs) that no preview adds up: the Zacks and Investing previews quote only the $80.6M backlog.
findings.independence: The order PRs are separate company documents: https://www.aehr.com/2026/08/aehr-receives-22-million-follow-on-order-for-ai-processor-wafer-level-burn-in-systems/ (2026-08-12) and https://www.aehr.com/2026/10/aehr-receives-follow-on-sonoma-production-orders-for-lead-hyperscale-customer-s-next-generation-ai-processor/ (2026-10-07). The Q4 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15228507339449344) gives the $20M transition-period bookings, and the CFO said Q1 'pretty good', Q2 'going to be a big quarter'. All are company sources, so the finding counts once. Caveat: backlog has slipped at Aehr before (FY2025).

findings.finding: Teradyne's 2026-10-06 launch of burn-in on its Titan HP platform set off the leg down (about $100 to $73 within a week, $53 now). The day after, 2026-10-07, Aehr's lead hyperscale Sonoma customer placed ~$6M of follow-on production orders for its next-generation AI processor, shipping to a Taiwan OSAT over six months. The 2026-11-02 call is management's first chance to address the competitive question in public. Titan HP is a package/system-level product; it overlaps Sonoma (about $50M of the FY27 guide per the CEO) more than FOX wafer-level burn-in.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a competitor. The closest precedent is the 2025-10-06 print (-17.38%), where the hyperscaler/AI deal news did not offset weak revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: The price holds the bear case. A ~$1.7B cap on a $130-150M guide after a 49% drop, with downside paid in the skew, is what a share-loss narrative looks like. If the market had absorbed the re-order and the wafer-level vs. package-level distinction, the stock would have stabilised after Oppenheimer's 2026-10-14 note; it fell another ~27%. That cuts both ways: the sell-side rebuttal is public and did not work, so only management's own words, or a reaffirmed or raised guide, can move it, and this finding is sized for that.
findings.independence: Teradyne PR (https://stockhouse.com/news/press-releases/2026/10/06/teradyne-introduces-titan-hp-platform-with-burn-in-capabilities-for-advanced-ai, 2026-10-06; Titan HP 'available now and deployed in production'). Aehr's Oct 7 order PR (https://www.aehr.com/2026/10/aehr-receives-follow-on-sonoma-production-orders-for-lead-hyperscale-customer-s-next-generation-ai-processor/). Oppenheimer's argument (https://finimize.com/content/oppenheimer-says-aehrs-selloff-misses-a-key-testing-detail). The Oct 7 PR is also counted in the backlog finding: shared document, different claim (no displacement vs. order coverage).

findings.finding: Crowded short into the print: 18.05% of float short (5.62M shares, settlement 2026-10-15, up 7.7%), 2.0 days to cover, after a 49% 20-day decline and 63% off the high. A reaffirmed guide gives a squeeze mechanism the option skew does not price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest was also ~18.8% in Sept 2025 (MarketBeat). The prints that followed were mixed: -17.38% (2025-10-06), then +15.95%, +25.69% and +21.91% on the next three.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, but the skew (+11.75, downside paid) and put/call OI of 0.5 show option buyers paying for further downside, not for a squeeze. Low days to cover (2.0) on ~2.6M shares a day means covering can be fast and violent.
findings.independence: Baseline tape: run_up_20d -48.97%, pct_from_52w_high -63.41% (sealed baseline). Same direction, different source.

findings.finding: Margin pressure on the Q1 EPS bar ($0.10-0.11): the CEO said on the Q4 call that power-supply makers 'have raised their prices 40%', and FY26 non-GAAP gross margin fell to 38.5% from 44%. The Zacks preview flags component availability and shipment timing as a Q1 risk and puts Earnings ESP at 0%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin has not been the line this stock traded on. Bookings and backlog dominated the last three reactions; FY26's margin decline did not stop the +21.91% on 2026-07-14.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS has not moved in 30 days (Zacks) while revenue is expected to grow ~43% sequentially, so a margin squeeze from component costs is not in the estimate path. It is small because this stock trades on orders, not margin.
findings.independence: Zacks preview (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:92d98440e094b:0-aehr-gears-up-to-report-q1-earnings-what-s-in-store-for-the-stock/) repeats the power-supply price point, so this is largely the same company statement.

findings.finding: Peer demand read after Aehr last spoke: Advantest raised its full-year forecast on 2026-10-28, citing SoC test sales driven by AI-related production volume and complexity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of AEHR reacting to Advantest prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy only. AEHR fell further after it (gap down 2026-10-30), so the market did not carry the peer's AI-test strength over to Aehr; it will only matter if Aehr's own bookings confirm it.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a counterparty. Teradyne's Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097210/000119312526434981/ter-ex99_1.htm) beat with AI >60% of sales, but see the next finding for its caution.

findings.finding: Teradyne's 2026-10-28 call called compute 'at its lowest within Q3', a 'digestion period' after a record quarter, and ASIC programs 'more back half loaded' in 2027. Aehr's Sonoma and wafer-level AI revenue sits on hyperscaler ASIC/AI-processor ramps, so order timing could slip.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Order-timing slips drove -12.39% (2025-07-08) and -17.38% (2025-10-06), but those were tariff-related.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy from a competitor's tester business. Partly priced: AEHR gapped down 2026-10-30 ($61.21 to $54.17 open) two days after this call, with no company news found.
findings.independence: Proxy; Teradyne is a competitor, not a counterparty. Aehr's own Oct 7 order PR points the other way for the lead hyperscaler.

findings.finding: Insiders sold about $63.3M across 49 filings in the 12 months to 2026-10-26 with no open-market purchases. The October 2026 Form 4 cluster is all RSU tax withholding (e.g. A. Sporck, 188 shares, code F, $63.95, 2026-10-27), so no insider bought the 49% decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Large August 2026 sales at $127-141 (CEO 40,000 shares at $130.84 on 2026-08-12) preceded the peak; no measured print reaction tied to insider flow.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and stale. Sized near zero because absence of insider buying is weak evidence.
findings.independence: Aggregate figure from https://massive.com/quote/aehr/insider-trading; filing list at https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001040470&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40

findings.finding: Part of the drawdown is sector beta, not Aehr news: the Philadelphia Semiconductor index fell 11.4% in the week ending 2026-10-16 on rate-hike repricing and AI build-out cost worries, and chip/AI names were bouncing premarket on 2026-11-02 (AEHR +3.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro. Small: it explains part of the drop but does not say the stock is mispriced.

baseline_tension: The findings lean positive against a +11.75 put skew and a -49% 20-day run-up. Why the option market might be wrong here: the downside it pays for is the Titan HP share-loss story, and Aehr's own documents (Sonoma re-order the day after the launch, orders covering ~the low end of the guide) cut against it. The skew still gets weight because the Oppenheimer rebuttal failed, so p_up is 57 rather than 60+.
lessons_applied: Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the Titan HP rebuttal finding cut from +3.0 to +2.0, because its own why_not_priced notes that Oppenheimer's identical public rebuttal on 2026-10-14 failed to stop a further ~27% fall.

Lesson 7 (positioning, sign against skew): p_up moved 60 -> 57 against the +11.75 put skew, with the explicit reason the option market may be wrong stated in baseline_tension; the crowded-short finding trimmed +2.0 -> +1.5 as a mechanism rather than a predicted reaction (lesson 1).
Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0, and the 'it is cheap' inference): the sector-beta finding trimmed +0.5 -> +0.3.

Last section (baseline_history_trustworthy false): checked the reaction history; the 7 dates are real releases (2026-07-14 Q4 PR, 2026-04-07 Q3 call, 2025-10-06 Q1 FY26 -17%), and the fiscal-year change only moves the quarter boundary, so the 21.9% median stands as the base rate. abs_move_pct left at 20.

Left standing: the guide-coverage finding (a company-level number from primary documents, lesson 'what has worked'), the margin finding, the two peer proxies (filed small per lesson 5), and the insider finding.
